# Volume 1 — CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

WHEN Nell opened her eyes and sat up in bed, it was broad daylight, and she gazed bewilderedly toward the window, where a torrent of bright sunlight streamed in, while beyond it a pale, feathery object fluttered against patches of blue sky.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0000 }

Briefly, she was unable to recall her surroundings. An enjoyable sensation occurred initially, like something exceedingly nice; subsequently, a dreadful memory returned. She was at Grey Shutters, where her presence was undesired simply because she failed to be a boy!
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0001 }

However, morning had arrived, and indeed, a cherry-tree covered in blossoms stood right past her window. Leaping from her bed, she hurried over the floor. She shoved the sash upward—it moved with a stiff, creaking resistance, appearing as though it had not been raised in ages, which was true; moreover, it jammed so firmly that no support was required to keep it elevated.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0002 }

Nell fell to her knees and stared out at the June morning, her eyes shining with joy. Oh, was it not beautiful? Was it not a wonderful location? What if she was not actually going to remain here! She would pretend she was. There was room for imagination in this place.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0003 }

An enormous cherry-tree stood outdoors, positioned so near that its branches struck the building, and it was so densely covered in blooms that almost no leaves could be observed. Adjacent to the house on either side lay a large orchard, comprising apple-trees on one side and cherry-trees on the other, which were likewise covered in a shower of blossoms; moreover, dandelions were scattered throughout their grass. Within the garden underneath stood lilac-trees heavy with purple blooms, and the morning breeze carried their intoxicatingly sweet scent up toward the window.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0004 }

A verdant meadow thick with clover inclined downward beneath the garden toward the basin that contained the flowing brook and dozens of pale birches, which rose lightly from a carpet of bushes hinting at wonderful prospects of ferns, moss, and broad forest flora. Past that lay a ridge, verdant and soft with spruce and fir trees; an opening cut through it, revealing the gray gable end of the small dwelling she had noticed from the opposite bank of the Lake of Glassy Waters.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0005 }

To the left stood the large barns, and past them, further down across low-sloping green fields, the blue sea could be seen sparkling.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0006 }

The beauty-loving eyes of Nell lingered upon the entire scene, absorbing each detail with greed. So many unlovely places had been beheld by her in her life, poor child; nevertheless, this was as lovely as any place she had ever dreamed of.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0007 }

She remained on her knees, unaware of anything except the beauty surrounding her, before a hand upon her shoulder frightened her. Unnoticed by the little dreamer, Thirza had entered.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0008 }

“You ought to be dressed by now,” she stated in a abrupt manner.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0009 }

Thirza truly lacked the knowledge of how to converse with the little girl, and this awkward lack of understanding caused her to be sharp and abrupt when that was not her intention.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0010 }

Rising to her feet, Nell took a deep breath.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0011 }

“Oh, isn’t it wonderful?” she said, making a broad gesture with her hand toward the pleasant world beyond.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0012 }

“The tree is large,” Thirza stated, “and its blossoms are grand, but its yield is never worth anything—it is tiny and full of worms.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0013 }

“Oh, I am not referring solely to the tree; naturally it is beautiful—yes, it is dazzlingly beautiful—it flowers as though it really intended to—however I was referring to all of it, the garden along with the orchard, the stream, and the forest, the entire immense beloved world. Do you not feel a deep affection for the world on a morning such as this? Furthermore, I am able to hear the stream laughing all the way to this spot. Did you ever observe how joyful streams are? They laugh constantly. I have even heard them beneath the ice during the winter. I am exceedingly pleased that a stream is located close to Grey Shutters. You might suppose it matters nothing to me since you do not plan to keep me, yet it does matter. It will always bring me pleasure to recall that a stream exists at Grey Shutters, even should I fail to behold it ever again. Were there no stream, I would be plagued by the uneasy sensation that one should exist. I am not plunged into deep despair this morning. Morning never allows me to be. Is it not a marvelous reality that mornings exist? Nevertheless, I feel extremely mournful. I was merely picturing that I was actually the person you desired after all and that my stay here would endure for ever and ever. That provided immense solace while it endured. Yet the most painful aspect of picturing things is the arrival of the moment when stopping becomes necessary, and that causes pain.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0014 }

“It would be best for you to put on your clothes and descend the stairs, ignoring your fancies,” Thirza remarked the moment she found an opportunity to speak. “The morning meal is ready. Clean your face and brush your hair. Keep the window raised and fold your bedding over the bed’s end. Hurry as much as possible.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0015 }

It was clear that Nell was capable of being prompt when necessary, as she appeared on the lower floor within ten minutes, wearing neatly arranged garments, with her hair combed and plaited, her face cleansed, and her mind filled with a satisfying sense that she had satisfied every one of Thirza’s demands. Actually, though, turning down her bedding was something she had neglected to do.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0016 }

“This morning, I have quite an appetite,” she declared while sliding onto the seat that Thirza held out for her. “Last night, the world felt like a howling wilderness, but it doesn’t seem that way anymore. It makes me happy that the sun is shining this morning. Even so, rainy mornings are also very much to my liking. Every kind of morning holds interest, wouldn’t you agree? What the day will bring remains unknown, leaving vast room for imagination. Still, I am pleased about the lack of rain today, since maintaining cheerfulness and enduring suffering comes more easily under a sunny sky. I sense that I have quite a lot to endure. Reading about griefs and picturing yourself facing them with courage is fine and good, yet experiencing them in reality is not nearly as pleasant, is it?”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0017 }

“In the name of mercy, keep quiet,” Thirza said. “For a young girl, your speech is altogether excessive.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0018 }

At that point Nell became quiet so dutifully and completely that her ongoing lack of speech rendered Thirza somewhat uneasy, as though she were in the company of a thing that was not quite normal. Obed likewise remained silent,—though this was customary,—with the result that the dinner proved to be extremely quiet.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0019 }

As the meal went on, Nell grew increasingly preoccupied, consuming her food automatically while her large eyes remained constantly glued to the firmament beyond the glass, seeing nothing. Thirza grew increasingly anxious because of this; a distressing sensation came over her that although the strange youngster's physical form was present at the board, her soul had traveled off to a distant, lofty cloud realm, carried high by imaginative wings. Who could desire a youngster like that in the house?
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0020 }

Still, among all unthinkable desires, Obed desired to retain her! Thirza sensed his longing for it was no less strong this morning than it had been on the previous evening, and that his desire would persist. Such was Obed's manner—to adopt a caprice and adhere to it with an astonishingly quiet stubbornness—a stubbornness whose very quietness rendered it tenfold more powerful and successful than if he had given it voice.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0021 }

Once she had finished eating, Nell emerged from her deep thought and volunteered to do the washing up.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0022 }

“Are you able to clean plates properly?” inquired Thirza with suspicion.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0023 }

“Fairly well. However, I am superior at caring for young ones. I possess a great deal of practice in doing so. It is a terrible shame that you do not have any in this place for me to care for.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0024 }

“I do not think that I desire any additional youngsters to care for beyond those currently in my charge. In all honesty, you present a sufficient challenge. I am at a loss as to what should be done regarding you. Obed is an utterly absurd person.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0025 }

“I consider him wonderful,” Nell remarked with disapproval. “He displays such great empathy. The extent of my speaking didn't bother him—it appeared to please him. The very moment I laid eyes on him, I sensed that our souls were aligned.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0026 }

“If being kindred spirits implies being peculiar, the two of you certainly fit the description,” Thirza declared, sniffing. “Indeed, the dishwashing is permitted. Utilize an abundance of heated water, and ensure they are thoroughly wiped dry. My schedule is full today because I must journey to Pale Sands later today to meet Mrs. Tranter. Your presence will be required beside me so we can determine your future arrangements. Upon completing the kitchen work, proceed to the upper level to tidy your bedding.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0027 }

Thirza observed the process with a vigilant gaze and recognized that Nell cleaned the plates with sufficient skill. Subsequently, the girl was not as adept at making her bed, since the skill of dealing with a feather mattress had never been taught to her. Nevertheless, the task was eventually accomplished and flattened out; whereupon Thirza, wishing to be free of her presence, informed her that she could venture outside and entertain herself until it was time for dinner.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0028 }

Nell rushed toward the door, her face radiant and her eyes shining. Right at the threshold she halted abruptly, turned completely around, returned and took a seat beside the table, her radiance and shine extinguished as thoroughly as though a person had placed a snuffer over her.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0029 }

“What is wrong this time?” Thirza asked.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0030 }

“I don’t dare go out,” Nell stated, sounding like a martyr giving up every joy on earth. “Unless I am permitted to remain in this place, loving Grey Shutters is pointless. Furthermore, should I venture outside and become familiar with every one of those trees and blossoms, as well as the orchard and the stream, I will inevitably fall in love with it all. The situation is difficult enough already, so I refuse to increase the difficulty. I have a strong desire to venture outside—all things appear to be shouting to me, ‘Nell, Nell, come out to us. Nell, Nell, we want a playmate’—yet abstaining is the wiser choice. Loving anything is useless if one must be ripped away from it, wouldn't you say? Besides, preventing oneself from loving things is terribly difficult, isn't it? For that reason, I felt such joy upon believing I would reside in this home. I assumed I would possess numerous objects to love without any obstacles stopping me. However, that fleeting fantasy has ended. Now that I have accepted my destiny, I believe I will avoid going outside lest I become unresigned once more. Could you tell me the name of the geranium sitting on the window-sill?”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0031 }

“The apple-scented geranium is what that is.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0032 }

“Oh, that isn't the kind of name I am referring to. I am asking about a name you invented for it on your own. Hasn't a name been provided by you? Is it permissible for me to bestow a name upon it, in that case? Might I refer to it as—let me think—Bonny could work—could I speak of it as Bonny for the duration of my stay? Oh, please allow me to!”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0033 }

“Gracious, it doesn't matter to me. Still, why in the world would anyone bother giving a name to a geranium?”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0034 }

“Oh, even when they are just geraniums, I prefer items to possess names. They appear more like individuals that way. How can you be sure a geranium’s feelings aren't wounded merely by being referred to as a geranium and nothing more? It wouldn't suit you to be addressed as merely a woman constantly. Yes, Bonny will be its name. This morning, I gave a name to that cherry-tree beyond my bedroom window. Frost Maiden was what I called it owing to its extreme whiteness. To be sure, its blossoms will not last forever, but it is possible to pretend they do, isn't it?”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0035 }

“Never in my whole life have I seen or heard anything that equals her,” Thirza muttered, retreating down into the cellar to fetch potatoes. “Obed is right that she is sort of interesting. Already I can feel myself wondering what in the world her next words will be. It won't be long before she casts a spell over me as well. Obed is already under it. That glance he threw my way on his way out repeated every single thing he stated or suggested yesterday evening. I wish he possessed the traits of normal men and would discuss matters fully. Then a person could reply and use logic to persuade him. However, how can anyone handle a man who merely stares?”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0036 }

When Thirza came back from her journey to the cellar, Nell, who had her chin resting in her hands and her gaze fixed on the sky, had fallen back into a dream. Thirza then departed from her side until the early dinner was served on the table.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0037 }

“Obed, am I able to take the mare and buggy later today?” asked Thirza.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0038 }

Nodding his head, Obed cast a longing glance toward Nell, which Thirza cut across before speaking sternly:
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0039 }

“I am heading over to Pale Sands to get this matter sorted out. Nell will accompany me, and it is likely that Mrs. Tranter will arrange her immediate return to Nova Scotia. After I prepare your tea and leave it out for you, I will return in time for the cow milking.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0040 }

Obed remained silent, which made Thirza feel as though her words and breath had been spent in vain. A man who refuses to respond is the ultimate source of annoyance—with the sole exception of a woman who behaves the same way.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0041 }

In good time, Obed tackled the sorrel to the buggy, whereupon Thirza and Nell departed. Obed unlatched the yard gate for their exit, and while they navigated it at a walk, he remarked, apparently to no one specifically:
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0042 }

“Young Tobias Buote from the Creek came by earlier today, and I informed him that I thought I would take him on for the summer season.”
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0043 }

Thirza remained silent, yet she struck the unfortunate sorrel with the whip so fiercely that the chubby mare, unaccustomed to such handling, dashed furiously down the lane at a terrifying speed. As the buggy jolted forward, Thirza glanced behind her a single time and observed that irritating Obed bent over the gate, gazing mournfully in their direction.
{: #nw-v01-c04-p0044 }
